key_insight: Shrinkage priors combined with generalized Bayes offer a sample-efficient way to train neural implicit generative models by promoting sparse parameter representations.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets data-limited settings where neural model parameter counts greatly exceed available training samples.
method: Replace the intractable likelihood with a posterior based on a strictly proper scoring rule.
Apply sparsity-inducing shrinkage priors to regularize model parameters.
Use block stochastic-gradient MCMC within Gibbs sampling to explore the high-dimensional posterior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on linear regression with far more parameters than samples and an application to neural generative models, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: High-dimensional posterior sampling requires careful convergence checks; the abstract does not establish computational cost or scalability.
paper_title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models
